To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a semantic federated engine that is able to transparently perform federated queries and that it can be used for retrieving domain-specific documents.

1) the semantic search engine developed by our team can be considered a proof of concept of a semantic federated system, which is able to perform transparent federated queries over different repositories; 2) the semantic search platform developed in the context on the EU project is able to provide semantic search functionalities to the end users, by means of a user interface; 3) the platform is able to provide a set of functionalities that allow users and third parties to manage and maintain the platform.

(1) a semantic federated system is feasible, (2) the use of a general-purpose ontology for describing the content of repositories is a viable solution for the construction of a knowledge graph, (3) the use of the Linked Open Data cloud as the main repository of ontologies is a feasible solution, and (4) the developed system is able to provide a good level of accuracy and precision for the retrieval of relevant documents.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a) the development of a platform for federated semantic search, b) the definition of a methodology for building knowledge graphs describing the contents of repositories, c) the definition of an ontology-based query transformation process for enriching user queries, and d) the definition of query expansion and ranking strategies for improving the quality of the retrieved documents.
the development of an infrastructure for the construction of domain-specific federated search engines.
the development of an open-source platform, which can be easily extended by adding new knowledge graphs and new domain-specific repositories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the developed platform is a good example of a semantic federated IR system, which is able to perform transparent federated queries, and at the same time to exploit semantic knowledge for query enrichment and refinement.

our platform provides the possibility to perform semantic federated searches over a large number of repositories in a completely transparent way, while at the same time exploiting the knowledge contained in the connected repositories for enriching user queries.
the proposed approach is an interesting solution for the development of semantic federated search engines, but further work is needed to improve the quality of its semantic search component.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a platform for federating domain-specific search engines and we provided a solution for enriching user queries with semantic knowledge, thus improving the retrieval process.
the proposed platform is a semantic federated IR engine that can be used to retrieve documents from a set of repositories, while exploiting semantic knowledge in order to enrich the user queries.
we are able to perform semantic federated searches on a set of repositories without requiring any knowledge of their internal structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the developed platform is able to provide users with a semantic federated service, while keeping a reasonable level of complexity.

, by using a knowledge graph, the search engine is able to provide users with more precise answers, while the knowledge graph is incrementally enriched through the interaction of users with the search engine.
a semantic search engine can be developed without the need of creating a full ontology covering all the possible domains of interest.
